Commentary.Commentary: With Harry Brook and his teammates celebrating their ODI series win, the stage is set for the next chapter: the T20I series! The action resumes on June 6th at 5:30 pm GMT, with pre-match coverage starting an hour earlier. Stay tuned for more cricketing excitement between England and West Indies! Cheers!

England captain Harry Brook praised his team's dominant performance, highlighting the impressive start at Edgbaston and the big win. He commended the lower-order batting, particularly mentioning Will Jacks, and also gave credit to Jacob Bethell. Brook expressed satisfaction with the team's overall performance, noting that the players' contributions with the ball and bat bring depth and can only improve further. He emphasized that winning as a unit is key and was pleased with the team's efforts.

West Indies captain Shai Hope highlighted the positives from the series, singling out standout performers like Keacy Carty for his consistent form and Alzarri Joseph for picking up crucial wickets. Hope praised Joseph's skill, noting that he sometimes plays like he's in a video game. He emphasized the need for a mix of experienced players and new talent to perform well and acknowledged that the team needs to win many games to secure automatic qualification.

Joe Root is the Player of the Series. Root attributed his success to consistency in practice and thinking ahead of the opposition. He emphasized the importance of expanding the game and adapting his skills to the situation. Root expressed his desire to extend his current run, but noted that a break might be necessary soon due to the upcoming hectic schedule of Test matches.

Jamie Smith is the player of the match. Smith says that he was thrilled to have given his team a solid start at his home ground. He enjoyed the freedom to play his natural game and said that the team's support has been fantastic. Smith felt that he and his teammates complement each other well, and it's great when things go their way. After missing out in Cardiff, he was delighted to perform well at this match.
Stay tuned for the presentation ...

Earlier in the game, West Indies, despite early setbacks, posted a decent enough total, thanks to Sherfane Rutherford's 70 and Gudakesh Motie's 63, who added a 91-run partnership with Alzarri Joseph (41 off 29 balls). Adil Rashid took 3 wickets for 40 runs, while the England pace trio of Saqib Mahmood, Brydon Carse, and Matthew Potts also chipped in with a couple of wickets each.

West Indies' bowling fell short, largely due to Jamie Smith's explosive batting, which gave them little chance to get back into the game. Alzarri Joseph, Roston Chase, and Gudakesh Motie each took a wicket, while the other bowlers went wicketless.

England cruised to victory, thanks to a blistering start from Jamie Smith, who smashed 64 off just 28 balls, crushing West Indies' hopes of a comeback. The rest of the batting lineup chipped in, ensuring a comfortable win in the rain-shortened match.

England's new captain, Harry Brook, celebrates his leadership debut with a 3-0 whitewash over West Indies! Jos Buttler wraps up the 3rd ODI in style with a six to see his side home by a 7-wicket victory.
